paper_metadata.title: Strengthening of a CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy by carbide precipitation

evidence.quote: The equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) exhibits outstanding toughness and excellent strength-ductility combination at cryogenic temperatures.
Two HEAs with compositions of Cr 20 Mn 20 Fe 20 Co 20 Ni 20 (at.%) and Cr 19.68 Mn 19.68 Fe 19.68 Co 19.68 Ni 19.68 Nb 0.8 C0.8 (at.%) were prepared by arc melting

We will refer to the first of the above alloys as the base HEA and the second alloy to which Nb and C were added as the 0.8 Nb/C HEA.

parameters.atmosphere: high-purity argon, Ar backfilled to ~5×10^4 Pa after evacuation to ~5×10^-2 Pa

other.getter: small piece of pure Ti melted to getter residual oxygen

process_steps.input_state: raw materials mixture of pure Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Nb, Mn and Cr3C2 powder

evidence.quote: prepared by arc melting mixtures of the pure metals Cr, Fe, Co, Ni and Nb (purity >99.9 wt.%), Mn (purity >99 wt.%) and Cr 3C2 powder (purity >99 wt.%) in a high-purity argon atmosphere.
the alloys were melted. The buttons were flipped and remelted five times to ensure chemical homogeneity before drop-casting into a rectangular copper mold measuring 10 × 17 × 70 mm 3.
The ingots were sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, homogenized first at 1473 K for 24 h
and then at 1523 K for another 2 h followed by water quenching (WQ).

parameters.deformation: 88% reduction in thickness, final thickness ~1.2 mm

evidence.quote: the ingots were cold rolled along their long axis to a final thickness of ~1.2 mm, corresponding to a reduction in thickness of 88%.
The rolled sheets were annealed for 1 h at 1073 K to obtain fully recrystallized microstructures, followed by WQ.

attributes.size: nanoscale; dav = 42 nm; average precipitate size 42 nm
attributes.morphology: nanoscale particles, core-shell structure, coherent with FCC matrix
attributes.composition: core enriched in Nb (30.3 at.% Nb); shell contains Cr in addition to Nb (26.7 at.% Nb)

evidence.quote: the XRD pattern of the 0.8 Nb/C HEA (Fig. 2 c) exhibits peaks corresponding to the NbC phase in addition to the FCC peaks. The detection of the NbC phase by XRD indicates that it is present in a significant amount (>2% by volume).

attributes.composition: enriched in Cr and C, also containing other constituent elements

evidence.quote: A few particles enriched in Cr and C and also containing the other constituent elements were occasionally detected and confirmed to be M 23 C6 by TEM (not shown here).

evidence.quote: Fig. 3 a is a representative TEM BF micrograph of a particle in the 0.8 Nb/C HEA some of which show a core-shell structure. Chemical analysis by TEM EDX indicated that the core is enriched in Nb, while the outer shell contains Cr in addition to Nb (Table 1).

Higher magnification views of a deformation twin (~ 40 nm in thickness) are shown in the TEM BF image (Fig. 5 c) and the corresponding DF image (Fig. 5 d). The SAD pattern clearly shows the twin spots (inset in Fig. 5 d).

attributes.morphology: well developed cells with dense dislocation walls

evidence.quote: A lower magnification overview of the deformed structure is presented in Fig. 5 a, well developed cells with dense dislocation walls are clearly seen, similar to what has been seen before in the CrMnFeCoNi HEA [84].

attributes.morphology: pile-ups against grain/twin boundaries and particles

evidence.quote: Grain boundaries and particles are known to impede slip and, consistent with this, dislocation pile-ups can be seen to form against them (Fig. 4 a).
The fracture surface of the 0.8 Nb/C HEA after tensile testing at 293 K is covered with ductile dimples as shown in Fig. 6.
Coarser, microscale carbides (NbC and M 23 C6) were observed on the grain boundaries.
The yield strength of the 0.8 Nb/C HEA is ~732 MPa, which is roughly double that of the base HEA

Dislocation segments between particles are curved indicative of pinning by the particles followed by Orowan bowing. Thus, in the early stage of plastic deformation, the dislocations bypass the NbC particles by the classical Orowan bowing mechanism leaving behind dislocation loops around the particles.
The precipitation strengthening mechanism is the Orowan bowing and dislocation bypass mechanism.
